# Featured Papers

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Structure Selection in Ionic Colloidal Crystals via Independent Charge Tuning](<https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.6c08143>)
*Steven van Kesteren, Shihao Zang, Cheuk W. Leung, Glen M. Hocky, Stefano Sacanna* <br>
Adding micromolar amounts of simple ionic surfactants to a fixed pair of oppositely charged colloids independently alters individual surface charges, deterministically driving self-assembly into diverse crystal lattices—including a previously unreported Li3Fe-like structure—through the competing effects of Coulombic attraction and like-charge repulsion.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Coherent structures in active flows on dynamic surfaces](<https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgag335>)
*Sreejith Santhosh, Cuncheng Zhu, Blase Fencil, Mattia Serra* <br>
A parameterization-free geometric framework operating directly on triangulated meshes uncovers hidden transport barriers and deformation patterns across biological and soft-matter systems, enabling new insights into morphogenesis and synthetic material programming.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Tall adhesions overcome cell surface steric interference and rescue antibody-dependent phagocytosis in macrophages](<https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78095-7>)
*Aymeric Chorlay, Aaron M. Joffe, Jared Huzar, Jaffar Hasnain, Caitlin E. Cornell, Phillip L. Geissler, Daniel A. Fletcher* <br>
Steric hindrance caused by dense, non-binding glycocalyx proteins is overcome through kinetic enhancement, a process wherein tall adhesion molecules re-engineer interface transition states to promote short receptor engagement in a tunable, density-dependent manner.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Fibers and Glasses are Competing Material States in FUS Protein Condensation](<https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.28.754945>)
*Liru Feng, Iain Muntz, Ryota Takaki, Lionel Ndamba, Martine Ruer-Gruß, Frank Jülicher, Louise Jawerth* <br>
Protein fiber growth occurs overwhelmingly in the dilute phase surrounding condensates rather than inside them, establishing that glassy condensates and fibers are distinct, coexisting solid-like phases that do not directly interconvert.
:::

:::
